title: Even-length parity language is logarithmic-space decidable
statement: The language of Boolean strings containing an even number of true bits is decidable in logarithmic space: there are a natural-number constant $c$ and a finite Turing machine such that, on every input $x$, the machine halts with the one-bit output indicating whether $x$ belongs to that language, using at most $c(\lfloor\log_2 |x|\rfloor+1)$ work-tape cells under the stated space measure.
